data.name: Roberto
data.gender_notes: Roberto is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'Robertus', which is a compound name consisting of 'Roth-', meaning 'bright', and 'Berth-', meaning 'famous'. In the Middle Ages, it was a popular name for male children, often given in honor of St. Robert of Molesmes. The name Roberto carries the meaning “Bright, famous” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Roberto usually hope their child will grow to embody bright, famous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the radiant brightness of faith and the fame of following God.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Roberto total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_greek.name: Ρομπέρτο

in_latin.name: Roberto

It is associated with the glory and light of God, expressing trust in God's providence. Historically, the name has been popularized by various saints and nobles, symbolizing spiritual illumination and divine favor. In Christian tradition, Roberto signifies a person of virtuous character, illuminated by God's presence.

data.cultural_impact: The name Roberto has been given to generations of individuals in various parts of the world, most notably in Spain, Portugal, Italy, and the Americas. The fame of the name is attributed to the many historical figures who have carried it, such as Roberto Clemente, a legendary baseball player from Puerto Rico and Saint Roberto Belarmino, a 16th-century Italian Jesuit. The name's association with brightness and fame continues to inspire and influence individuals and communities today.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Roberto holds a significant spiritual meaning for Christians, as it is derived from the Latin names 'Roth-' and 'Berth-'. 'Roth-' signifies the light and brightness of God, while 'Berth-' represents the fame or renown of the Lord. Thus, the name Roberto is a reminder of God's presence and the importance of bringing His light and fame to the world. As St. Robert of Molesmes once said, "God is not a distant deity, but a living, loving God who is intimately involved in every aspect of our lives." By embracing the spiritual significance of the name Roberto, we are called to reflect the light and Fame of God in all that we do.

He was a powerful and learned prince, known for his patronage of scholars and the arts. During his reign, he supported the development of Capua as a center of culture and learning.

Roberto de' Nobili, an Italian Jesuit priest, was born in 1577 in the Tuscan city of Florence. He claimed to have experienced a divine revelation that led him to believe he was a reincarnation of an Indian prince. He spent the rest of his life living among the locals in Madurai, India, and promoting the Catholic faith through his interactions with the local culture.
